description:
pkix-profiles/Cargo.toml:11

`pkix-profiles/Cargo.toml` declares:
```toml
categories  = ["cryptography"]
```

This is fine. But the crate's lib.rs doc comment explicitly states:
```
//! # `std` requirement
//!
//! This crate requires `std`. It does not support `no_std` in v0.1
```

While the categories don't include `no-std`, there is no missing `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]` guard in the crate root, which is correct. However, unlike `pkix-path` and `pkix-revocation`, `pkix-profiles` has no explicit `std` feature gate and doesn't warn users attempting `no_std` usage at compile time with a meaningful error.

Additionally, `pkix-profiles` depends on `pkix-path = { workspace = true }` without any feature flags. `pkix-path` defaults to enabling `rsa` and `p256` backends. This means `pkix-profiles` unconditionally pulls in the `rsa` and `p256` crates (large compile-time cost) even for users who want only the `smime_policy()` function.

Fix: Add an explicit dependency on `pkix-path` with `default-features = false` and enable only the features actually needed, or add a feature-gating mechanism.
title: pkix-profiles: no_std claim in categories but crate requires std
